summary: Both render a bottom-fed, upward-propagating cellular fire on a ~16-cell logical grid with the same red-orange palette family, but the port's flames are far taller and flatter, its wind sway is ~2x too fast and half the amplitude, its Speed dial runs backwards, and its DragonBreath mode is an intermittent dim burst where the original is a sustained white-hot plume.
observations: Alive on both sides: no compile or runtime errors, 16x16 grid rig, 0 zero-motion frames in a 30 s late window (--skip 40), brightnessTrend steady on both. Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false).

Survey over 60 s and again over 240 s at 5 fps shows ONE continuous regime on both sides — no mode rotation, no sparse events, no slow palette walk. Seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give statistically identical output on both sides (orig mean 10-11 / port mean 40-42), so nothing here is a one-seed fluke.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS diverge hard. Row profile (row 0 = top, row 15 = bottom, mean over 6 dumps in the 43-68 s window): orig `0 0 0 0 1 1 1 2 3 3 6 9 13 25 37 60` — flames confined to the bottom ~5 rows; port `17 20 17 19 24 24 28 33 38 41 47 53 62 76 84 96` — every row lit including the very top. Mean brightness orig 10.3 vs port 41.0 (~4x).

Most of that brightness gap is the colour picker's UNSET default value. With the picker set explicitly to (h=0.02, s=1, v) on both sides at FlameHeight=1, the two sides' mean brightness matches within 3%: v=0.4 -> 25.3/24.5, v=0.6 -> 38.1/36.9, v=0.8 -> 49.5/49.2. Untouched at the same dials the pair is 34 vs 59, implying the original's default picker value is ~0.55 while the port's sits at ~1.0.

FLAME HEIGHT is a genuine structural divergence, not a brightness artefact — with the picker pinned at (0.02,1,0.6) the port's whole FlameHeight curve is offset ~+0.3. Row profiles: FH=0 orig `...0 0 0 6` (bottom row only) vs port `...1 2 8 26` (bottom 4 rows); FH=0.5 orig `...0 1 5 23` (bottom 3 rows) vs port `0 0 0 1 1 2 2 4 6 8 12 13 19 25 34 50` (13 rows lit). Port FH=0.25 looks like orig FH~0.6; port FH=0.5 looks like orig FH~0.72.

Vertical falloff is much flatter on the port. At FH=1, picker-pinned: orig bottom row 88 -> row 1 = 22 (4x drop, hot base with a quick fade); port bottom row 64 -> row 0 = 24 (2.7x drop, nearly uniform wash).
The original NEVER lights the top grid row: at FH=1 its row 0 is exactly 0 while row 1 is 22. The port lights row 0 (24 at the same settings).

WIND SWAY rhythm is wrong. Brightness-weighted column centroid at default dials, dumped every 0.2 s over 24 s: orig traces a smooth sinusoid, range 4.84-9.99 columns, autocorrelation peak at 9.8 s. Port is jittery and low-amplitude, range 6.21-8.75, weak autocorrelation peak at 4.4 s. Same picture at explicit Wind=0 (orig half-period ~4.6 s / +-0.8 col; port full period ~4.0 s / +-0.45 col) — the rhythm images show it as one broad slow diagonal on the orig versus tight repeating chevrons on the port.

SPEED DIAL IS INVERTED. Fraction of frames whose output changed, 240 frames at 20 fps, FlameHeight=1/Wind=0.5: orig Speed=0 -> 240/240 (tick <=0.05 s, fastest), Speed=0.5 -> 80/240 (tick 0.15 s), Speed=1 -> 48/240 (tick 0.25 s, slowest); motion avg 10.3 / 3.4 / 2.1. Port Speed=0 -> 89/240 (tick ~0.135 s, slowest), Speed=0.5 -> 160/240 (tick ~0.075 s), Speed=1 -> 240/240 (fastest); motion avg 6.0 / 11.1 / 18.6. Higher Speed slows the original down and speeds the port up.

Both sides are frame-rate independent: rendering the same settings at 10, 20 and 40 fps reproduces the identical meanBrightness value sequence with each value held for 2 / 3 / 5 frames respectively (orig) and 1 / 2 / 3 frames (port). No frame-rate coupling on either side; the port's simulation tick is simply ~2x shorter than the original's at the same Speed value.

DRAGON MODE is qualitatively different. Orig sliderDragonMode >= ~0.6 gives a SUSTAINED, full-height, white-hot central plume that pulses (~6.4 s) but never goes dark — mean brightness 59 over a 16 s window, rhythm image shows continuous bright banding. Port toggleDragonBreath = 1 gives short dim orange bursts separated by multi-second FULLY BLACK gaps (~4 s cycle) — mean brightness 8 over the same window, rhythm image is mostly black. Orig turns dragon mode BRIGHTER than normal (33 -> 59); the port turns it DARKER (60 -> 8).

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH (both directions). Orig exposes `hsvPickerHue` (hsvPicker, label "Hue"), `sliderFlameHeight`, `sliderWind`, `sliderDragonMode` (slider, label "DragonMode"), `sliderSpeed`. Port exposes `hsvPickerColor` (hsvPicker, label "Color"), `sliderFlameHeight`, `sliderWind`, `sliderSpeed`, `toggleDragonBreath` (toggle, label "DragonBreath"). Two names differ and the dragon control's KIND differs (slider vs toggle). The original's slider is effectively binary with a threshold near 0.6 (0/0.25/0.5 all render mean 33; 0.75/1 both render mean 59), so the toggle is functionally close, but the name and kind are still a fidelity gap.

PALETTE is the right family but the port's ramp is desaturated. Binned by peak channel over a FH=1 window: at peak ~140 orig is (142,40,0) vs port (141,58,12); at peak ~207 orig is (207,88,8) vs port (206,109,45); at peak ~240 orig (241,127,23) vs port (235,133,63). The original stays a deep red-orange with essentially no blue until it whites out; the port lifts green and especially blue much earlier, reading as a paler, more washed orange. Confirmed independent of overall brightness (with the picker pinned at v=0.6 the orig's meanB is 1.0 and the port's is 7.0).

Hue rotation itself matches: setting the picker to (h,1,1) rotates the whole fire palette identically on both sides — h=0 gives orig (R129,G31,B1) / port (R118,G43,B12); h=0.33 gives orig (R1,G129,B29) / port (R12,G118,B41); h=0.66 gives orig (R26,G1,B129) / port (R39,G12,B118).
Both sides go completely black when the picker is set with value 0, i.e. they respond identically to a zero-value colour — matching degenerate behaviour.

Resolution independence MATCHES. Re-rendered at --grid 8x8 and --grid 48x48, both sides quantize to the same coarse logical cell size: mean identical-colour run length at 48x48 is orig 3.48 horizontal / 3.30 vertical and port 3.56 / 3.49, i.e. both draw into a fixed ~14-16 cell buffer and upscale rather than rasterizing at native resolution.

dials.name: hsvPickerHue (orig) / hsvPickerColor (port)
dials.origEffect: Rotates the entire fire palette to the chosen hue; the value component scales overall brightness (mean 25/38/50 at v=0.4/0.6/0.8). Unset default sits at roughly v~0.55.
dials.portEffect: Same hue rotation and same brightness scaling (mean 24/37/49 at the same v), but the unset default sits at roughly v~1.0, and the ramp carries noticeably more green and blue at every intensity (paler orange). Control name and label differ (Color vs Hue).

dials.name: sliderFlameHeight
dials.origEffect: Same direction — raises the flame column. 0 is essentially dead (bottom row only, mean 0.2, 87/120 zero-motion frames); 0.5 lights the bottom 2-3 rows; 1 fills rows 1-15 with a steep hot-base gradient (row 15 = 88, row 1 = 22).
dials.portEffect: Same direction but offset ~+0.3 and much flatter. 0 already lights the bottom 4 rows and animates continuously (mean 4, 1 zero-motion frame); 0.5 lights 13 rows; 1 fills all 16 rows almost uniformly (row 15 = 64, row 0 = 24).

dials.name: sliderWind
dials.origEffect: Increases the amplitude of a smooth horizontal sway without changing its period: at Wind=0 the column centroid swings ~+-0.8 col, at Wind=1 ~+-1.8 col, both on a ~9-10 s cycle that stays sinusoidal.
dials.portEffect: Increases amplitude too (~+-0.45 col at 0, ~+-1.0 col at 1), so direction matches, but the underlying cycle is ~4.0-4.4 s (roughly 2.3x too fast) and at Wind=1 the sway becomes jittery/turbulent rather than staying a clean sweep.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: INVERSE: higher value = slower. Simulation tick 0.05 s at Speed=0, 0.15 s at 0.5, 0.25 s at 1 (motion avg 10.3 / 3.4 / 2.1).
dials.portEffect: FORWARD: higher value = faster. Simulation tick ~0.135 s at Speed=0, ~0.075 s at 0.5, 0.05 s at 1 (motion avg 6.0 / 11.1 / 18.6). Direction is reversed and the usable range is narrower.

dials.name: sliderDragonMode (orig) / toggleDragonBreath (port)
dials.origEffect: Threshold near 0.6 (0/0.25/0.5 identical, 0.75/1 identical). When on, replaces the field with a sustained full-height white-hot central plume that pulses on a ~6.4 s cycle but never goes dark; mean brightness rises from 33 to 59.
dials.portEffect: Binary toggle. When on, produces short dim orange bursts separated by multi-second fully-black gaps on a ~4 s cycle; mean brightness DROPS from 60 to 8. Also a control-kind change (slider -> toggle) and a name/label change.

feedback: Reverse the Speed dial. On the original, Speed=0 is the FASTEST setting (simulation step every ~0.05 s) and Speed=1 the SLOWEST (~0.25 s); the port has it the other way round (0 -> ~0.135 s, 1 -> ~0.05 s). After flipping, also stretch the range: the original spans 0.05-0.25 s per step, the port only 0.05-0.135 s.

Lower the flame column across the whole FlameHeight range — the port's response is offset by about +0.3. Target row profiles (16-row grid, row 15 = bottom, colour picker pinned at h=0.02,s=1,v=0.6): FlameHeight=0 should be essentially dark except the bottom row (~6) and near-frozen; FlameHeight=0.5 should light only the bottom 2-3 rows (~0/1/5/23); FlameHeight=1 should read ~88 at the bottom falling to ~22 at row 1. The port currently posts 26 / 50 / 64 at the bottom with 13-16 rows lit at mid settings.

Steepen the vertical falloff. At full FlameHeight the original loses ~4x brightness from the bottom row to row 1 (hot base, quick fade); the port loses only ~2.7x from the bottom row to row 0, so it reads as a uniform orange wash instead of a fire with a hot base.
Do not light the top grid row. Even at FlameHeight=1 the original's row 0 is exactly 0 while row 1 is ~22 — the flame field stops one row short of the top. The port lights row 0 at ~24.

Slow the wind sway by ~2.3x and make it smooth. At default dials the original's brightness-weighted column centroid is a clean sinusoid with a 9.8 s period sweeping columns 4.8-10.0 of 16; the port wobbles over columns 6.2-8.8 with a ragged ~4.4 s period. Amplitude should also roughly double. Raising Wind should grow the amplitude while LEAVING THE PERIOD ALONE — the original stays sinusoidal at Wind=1 where the port turns turbulent.

Rework DragonBreath. The original's dragon mode is a SUSTAINED white-hot central plume that fills the grid height and never goes fully dark — its mean brightness nearly doubles versus normal mode (33 -> 59) and it pulses gently on a ~6.4 s cycle. The port's version is intermittent: brief dim orange bursts with multi-second black gaps, mean brightness 8 versus 60 in normal mode. It needs to be continuously lit, much brighter than normal fire, and white-hot at the core rather than a dark-gapped burst.

Desaturate less. At the same peak intensity the original's ramp keeps blue near zero and green low (peak ~140 -> RGB 142,40,0; peak ~207 -> 207,88,8); the port lifts both (141,58,12 and 206,109,45), which reads as a pale washed orange instead of a deep red-orange. Pull the green and especially the blue shoulder of the palette back until only the hottest pixels approach white.

Drop the colour picker's default value from ~1.0 to ~0.55. That single change removes most of the 4x default-brightness gap: with the picker set explicitly the two sides already match within 3% at v=0.4/0.6/0.8.

Control-surface fixes: rename `hsvPickerColor` to `hsvPickerHue` (label "Hue", not "Color") and `toggleDragonBreath` to `sliderDragonMode` (label "DragonMode", kind slider, engaging above ~0.6) to match the original's exposed controls exactly.

Already correct, don't regress: the bottom-fed upward cellular fire simulation, the hue-rotation behaviour of the colour picker (including going fully black at value 0), frame-rate independence, seed-independence, and resolution independence (both sides quantize to a ~14-16 cell logical buffer at 8x8 and 48x48).
